task_text: Moving fixture unlock: The left gripper starts around the handle of a free, hand-held fixture: a short channel with a ball inside, closed at its front by a spring-loaded latch gate, with a square socket on its side above the latch's push button. The left arm must grip the fixture and move it off its stand. While the fixture is still moving, the right arm must insert its peg into the socket, press the latch button down with the peg until the gate opens, and then pull the peg back out while the left hand keeps holding the fixture. The ball must then leave the fixture, run down a fixed inclined chute and come to rest in a basin at the chute's foot. The fixture must never be dropped. Phases, in order: moving_fixture_presentation: the left gripper grips the fixture body (both left-arm fingers in contact with it; contact with the latch does not count), while the fixture's frame origin is more than 0.018 m away from where it started and the fixture's centre of mass moves faster than 0.005 m/s.; relative_pin_insertion: the peg is inserted into the socket while the fixture keeps moving, for 0.06 s without interruption. Measured in the fixture frame, the peg tip (tool-frame point (0, 0, -0.07)) is within 5 mm horizontally of the socket's axis and 10-35 mm below the socket's top face (insertion depth 0.01 m < depth < 0.035 m; the socket itself is 30 mm deep). Meanwhile the left gripper still grips the fixture body and the fixture's centre of mass moves faster than 0.003 m/s.; mechanical_latch_open: the latch is pressed down by more than 17 mm (latch joint q < -0.017 m) at a moment when the peg tool touches the latch.; follow_and_withdraw: the peg tip is more than 15 mm above the socket's top face, measured along the fixture's z axis only (depth < -0.015 m, any lateral position). At the same moment the peg tool does not touch the latch and the left gripper still grips the fixture body.; gravity_delivery: after this phase has begun, the ball touches the chute; a chute contact before this phase does not count. After that, the ball rests in the basin for 0.7 s without interruption. Rests means: in the basin's frame (origin at the inner floor centre) its centre is within 0.0528 m of the centre along both x and y (0.45 x radius inside a 0.06 m half-width square) and between 0.012 m and 0.0381 m above the floor; it has touched the basin within the last 25 ms; and its speed is below 0.09 m/s. This completes the task. Goal geometry: Drop limit: the fixture's frame origin must stay at or above z = 0.18 m.
